clue.text: Indicate correct time

definitions.meaning: to mark something as right with a check mark
a moment, as in 'just a second'

explanation.definitionFit: A check mark shows an answer is right, and a brief instant is also called by the same word, as in 'back in a moment'.

clue.text: A terrible jam in forced halt is a feature of India

indicators.note: the shuffled jam with A goes inside the shuffled halt
forced here means twisted out of shape, so the letters of halt are rearranged
a terrible jam is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a dreadful traffic jam at an enforced stop somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work at once: 'forced' on halt and 'terrible' on jam, and 'in' places the second scramble, led by A, just after the first letter of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The marble mausoleum at Agra is one of India's best-known landmarks.

clue.text: Funny old note in volume

indicators.note: old and note are placed inside the abbreviation for volume

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An amusing old memo tucked inside a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like a book, but here it is CC, cubic centimetres.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes you laugh is humorous, an adjective sense of the word.

clue.text: A number joining right group in county

parts.note: some means an unspecified number of things
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Several people join a right-wing faction somewhere in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the English shires, in the West Country.

clue.text: Unusual description of constable on day of rest?

definitions.text: description of constable on day of rest?
definitions.meaning: a police officer not walking their regular patrol round is not on their beat

explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional things are quirky; and a constable who is not patrolling their round is away from the beat.

clue.text: Old writer's English narrative which gives credit to employee

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
a pen is a writing tool, so writer's gives pen's
an account is a story or report of events

explanation.surface: A story told in English by an old author, praising a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in writer's is dropped: PEN'S gives PENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms provide staff an allowance or card for work-related spending, reimbursed later.

clue.text: Soundly observe a sort of block in onshore wind

indicators.note: soundly signals the word for observe is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: to observe is to see
a breeze block is a light building block made from cinders and cement

explanation.surface: Advice to look carefully at a building block in the wind off the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE is spoken, giving SEA. A breeze block is a British building block of cinder concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle wind blowing from the ocean towards the land in the daytime.

clue.text: An outburst of plangent weeping is sickly sentimental

indicators.note: a few letters burst out from within the phrase plangent weeping

explanation.surface: A fit of mournful crying is cloyingly mawkish.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the word join: plangenT WEEping.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly dainty, quaint or saccharine, an informal British adjective.

clue.text: Show public display of clothing?

definitions.meaning: superficial display meant to impress, mere appearance
garments arranged in a shop front for passers-by

explanation.definitionFit: Merchants arrange clothes behind glass to attract shoppers, and by extension the phrase means a misleadingly attractive presentation.

clue.text: Bureau sends a bit of information to Cyprus

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
CY is the international code for Cyprus

explanation.surface: An office passes a snippet of news on to Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An office or organisation providing a service, such as a travel or news office.

clue.text: Certainly not getting on site though given a starting point

parts.note: someone leaping from a vehicle is plainly not boarding it
a site is a place

explanation.surface: Getting off a train rather than boarding it, yet given a point of departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A base from which an enterprise or journey is launched.

clue.text: Form of words in which civil engineer obscures time of mishap

indicators.note: the civil engineer covers up the time, standing in its place

parts.note: an accident is a mishap

explanation.surface: An engineer covers up when a mishap happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscures' puts CE where the T of ACCIDENT was.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, it is the part dealing with inflections, the changing shapes of words.

clue.text: Certainly not marine standard

parts.note: no is a firm refusal
RM, Royal Marines, the British naval infantry

explanation.surface: Seagoing practice is definitely not usual.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines, the UK's amphibious infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A usual or expected level or pattern of behaviour.

clue.text: Cunning method of entrance?

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A crafty way to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance passage under a curved structure, a way in under a vault.

clue.text: Savoury cake and game to note

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game with mallets and hoops
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pie and a game on the lawn worth writing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fried roll of mashed potato or minced meat coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: What golfer uses thrice has to show instability

parts.note: a golfer sets the ball on a tee
ter is Latin for three times, seen on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A golfer using something three times reveals a wobbly game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrice' tempts you to repeat TEE three times; it is the Latin word for 'three times'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble or sway unsteadily, as if about to fall.

clue.text: Force on street section changed from left to right

indicators.note: the letter for left is swapped for the letter for right

parts.note: a length is a section, as of pipe or cloth

explanation.surface: Traffic on a stretch of street is diverted to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed from left to right' turns LENGTH into RENGTH, with R for right in place of L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical power or might.

clue.text: University in river races will have no medal in this position

definitions.text: races will have no medal in this position

indicators.note: the university letter sits inside the river

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: University boat races on a river where one crew misses out on medals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth flows past Stirling into the Firth of Forth in Scotland. Only the first three places win medals.
explanation.definitionFit: The place just after bronze, missing the podium.

clue.text: Sigh of resignation seeing reduced elevation on house

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: height is elevation

explanation.surface: Someone sighs on seeing a house lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so house comes after the shortened elevation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of weary acceptance or boredom.

clue.text: Old worker restricts new French company

indicators.note: the worker holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a worker ant, a crossword staple
Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie

explanation.surface: An aged employee hampers a fresh French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the crossword's usual insect; 'restricts' means it hems in the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Very old, from long ago.

clue.text: Clever form of statue

indicators.note: form of signals the letters of statue are given a new shape

explanation.surface: A clever version of a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and sharp-witted.

clue.text: Bubbles on the water in south of France on top of sea

indicators.note: in this clue the French word is placed before the sea letter

parts.note: sud is French for south
S is a recognised abbreviation for sea

explanation.surface: Bubbles on the water down in the south of France at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' looks like the Riviera, but it is the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam or lather on washing water.

clue.text: Bring in amazing reduction

indicators.note: amazing suggests something mixed up and astonishing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An announcer touts an incredible price cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To present or bring something new into use.

clue.text: Bring together in university on empty Friday

indicators.note: empty means the inside of Friday is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Uniting people at college on a quiet Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: To join into one, to unite.

clue.text: Loose fellow leaves amusing party

indicators.note: the fellow departs, taken out of the party

parts.note: fun means amusing
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man walks out of a lively party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is a verb here, meaning to untie.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot is to unfasten it.

clue.text: All the same lacking status?

parts.note: not with means without, lacking
standing is status or rank

explanation.surface: Everything stays the same for a person without status.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless, in spite of that.

clue.text: Wild grove on terrace might well do this

definitions.text: Wild grove on terrace might well do this

indicators.note: wild means disorderly, so the letters of grove are scrambled

parts.note: a terrace is a row of houses

explanation.surface: An untamed clump of trees beside a terrace would spread across it.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrace is a British row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Untamed trees spread and cover neighbouring ground.

clue.text: It's not to be taken literally in writer's short article

definitions.text: It's not to be taken literally

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so writer's means my

indicators.note: short means the article loses its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A warning in an author's brief piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or fable, not literally true.
